title: Keeping the shop clean without stopping the day
target: How cleaning works in Supermarket Simulator: dirt as an object with a dirtiness mark, cleaning as a state with its own animations for floors and windows, handing the job to a janitor whose work runs as a routine, and the shop standing that cleanliness feeds into.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A shop that is open with customers coming in
A mop or a cleaning job you can hand over
Enough money for a hire if you are handing the work over

steps.do: Clean where the dirt actually is rather than wiping the whole shop evenly.
steps.because: dirt is placed as an object of its own in the shop, and the game marks how dirty something is, so the mess has a location (Dirt, DirtinessIndicator)

steps.do: Expect a cleaning job to be something that runs rather than something that happens.
steps.because: cleaning carries a tracked state of its own, which is why it can be interrupted and picked up again (CleaningState)

steps.do: Use the right job for the surface.
steps.because: mopping and window cleaning each have their own animation event, so a floor and a window are not the same task (MopCleaningAnimationEvent, WindowCleaningAnimationEvent)

steps.do: Hand the floors over when you cannot keep up with them yourself.
steps.because: there is a cleaning worker with a janitor item and a mop of their own, so the job can belong to somebody else (JanitorItem, Mop)

steps.do: Once a cleaner is hired, leave them to it rather than standing over them.
steps.because: the work is carried out by a routine of its own rather than waiting on you (CleaningForJanitorCoroutine)

steps.do: Treat hiring as a step of its own before you expect the shop to get cleaner.
steps.because: the people you employ are produced by the game through an employee generator (EmployeeGenerator)

steps.do: Expect a janitor to move through states rather than to wander and clean at random.
steps.because: the cleaning side carries a state machine and a state interface of its own (StateMachine, IState)

steps.do: Do not leave the mess for later just because it is not a sale.
steps.because: cleanliness is tracked against the shop's standing, so how clean the shop is becomes part of how it is judged (CleaningReputationManager)

steps.do: In a shared shop, expect one mop to be the mop for everybody.
steps.because: the mop has a networked interaction, so cleaning is a shared event rather than a local animation (NetworkMopInteraction)

commonMistakes: Letting dirt build up until it starts costing you standing.
Expecting a hired cleaner to take on the windows as well as the floors.
Treating cleaning as instant when it is a state that has to run.
Assuming cleanliness only matters visually rather than to the shop's standing.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
